title: Deploy SG/Send
one_line: The living deployment-documentation vault behind the deploy section of sgit.ai: seven target guides, two AWS runbooks, a scripts index and three reference pages, rendered from _page.json.
source: read-only clone of fyofmkvr from send.sgraph.ai; archived with 'sgit vault backup' (sgit-ai v0.15.0, no --include-key)

secret_audit.by: claude — mechanical sweep (scripts/audit_vault_export.sh) plus a full read of all 17 files
secret_audit.notes: Every mechanical hit is a documentation placeholder or a deploy-time generator, not a secret: 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=…' and 'AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…' (literal ellipses in a docker run example), '<acct>.dkr.ecr...' and 'Z...' and '<your-key>' and 'send.example.com' (placeholders), and 'AccessToken=$(openssl rand -hex 32)' (generates a value at deploy time). No AWS account IDs, ARNs, key IDs, tokens, private hostnames or PII. The only named third-party identifier is the public Docker Hub image 'diniscruz/sg-send-vault'. The docs' own security posture is that access tokens are startup parameters stored nowhere server-side, so there is little for the corpus to leak.

renders_via: _page.json (SG/Send page layout — hero, sections, cards, markdown includes)
notes: REFERENCE, not a copy: this vault is actively maintained (see its MAINTENANCE.md) and the endpoint serves the live version, so what a reader sees changes underneath them. vault.zip is a dated snapshot of 2026-08-17, not the canonical copy. Publishing a persistent read key differs from the share-token-per-release model the vault's own MAINTENANCE.md describes: a read key follows the vault forward, so every future revision is public from the moment it is pushed, and the key cannot be withdrawn. Flagged to the project lead on publication.
